title: Frontend: Array.prototype.reduce
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Array.prototype.reduce. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({values,operation,initial?}). Reduce values by add or multiply. Without initial, use the first item; empty without initial throws Empty reduction. initial is present only when Object.hasOwn says so.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Distinguish an omitted initial argument from an explicitly supplied undefined using argument count.
alternativeApproaches: Compare a focused array-only implementation with the complete specification requirements for generic receivers.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty without seed; explicit undefined seed; sparse array.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
